5	## Two test layers — the class suffix picks the Maven phase
6	
7	| Layer                 | Suffix  | Runs in         | Framework                                              | Skill                               |
8	|-----------------------|---------|-----------------|--------------------------------------------------------|-------------------------------------|
9	| Server-side view test | `*Test` | `./mvnw test`   | Vaadin Browserless (`SpringBrowserlessTest`)           | `aiup-vaadin-jooq:browserless-test` |
10	| Browser test          | `*IT`   | `./mvnw verify` | Playwright + Drama Finder (`AbstractBasePlaywrightIT`) | `aiup-vaadin-jooq:playwright-test`  |
11	
12	Surefire picks up `*Test`, Failsafe picks up `*IT` (both configured via `spring-boot-starter-parent`; the failsafe
13	plugin is declared in `pom.xml`). A browserless test named `*IT` or a Playwright test named `*Test` runs in the wrong
14	phase, and `TestLayerConventionsTest` fails the build when one does. The rule is worth enforcing because the
15	failure is otherwise silent: nothing errors, the wrong Maven plugin simply never picks the class up, and a test
16	that never runs reports as passing. Browserless is the default for use cases; Playwright is for test cases (`TC-*`) and
17	anything that genuinely needs a browser (client-side rendering, keyboard focus, scrolling).
18

20	
21	- **Vaadin Browserless Testing** (`browserless-test-junit6` + `browserless-test-spring`) is the default for Vaadin view
22	  tests — server-side, no
23	  browser, no servlet container.
24	  Reference: https://vaadin.com/docs/latest/flow/testing/browserless/getting-started
25	- View tests extend `PetClinicTestBase` (or `SpringBrowserlessTest` directly for tests that don't touch the DB, in
26	  which case add `@SpringBootTest` and `@Import(TestcontainersConfiguration.class)` yourself).

28	- **Use the `aiup-vaadin-jooq:browserless-test` skill** to scaffold a browserless test for a use case. Prefer it over

35	Tests that verify a use case are named after the use case, **not** the view. Format:
36	`UC<NNN><UseCaseNameInPascalCase>Test`, e.g `UC001ViewWelcomePageTest`, `UC004FindOwnersByLastNameTest`,

1	# Process View
2	
3	**Question:** How does the system behave at runtime?  
4	**Artifacts:** this document (sequence diagrams, transaction boundaries,
5	concurrency rules)  
6	**Notation:** Mermaid sequence diagrams, Markdown for rules  
7	**For the agent:** where a transaction begins and ends, what runs in the
8	background (nothing, today), and which races are accepted. Without this view an
9	agent quietly builds everything into one synchronous request — which happens to
10	be right here, but for reasons worth knowing.
11	
12	## Runtime shape
13	
14	One process. The UI is server-side: a browser event travels over the Vaadin
15	Flow protocol into the JVM, a view method runs, jOOQ statements go to
16	PostgreSQL, and the resulting UI change travels back. There is no REST layer,
17	no client-side state to keep in sync, and no second runtime.
18	
19	- **One view instance per navigation.** Route targets are Spring beans created
20	  per navigation; their state (the loaded owner, the form contents) lives in the
21	  user's session with the Vaadin `UI` until the user navigates away.
22	- **Repositories are singletons and stateless.** They hold a `DSLContext` and
23	  nothing else, so nothing about a user survives in them.
24	- **A user interaction is single-threaded.** Vaadin holds the session lock for
25	  the duration of the event, so two events of the same user never overlap.
26	
27	## Reading a screen — UC-005 View Owner Details
28	
29	```mermaid
30	sequenceDiagram
31	    actor U as Clinic User
32	    participant V as Owner details view
33	    participant OR as Owner queries
34	    participant PR as Pet queries
35	    participant VR as Visit queries
36	    participant DB as PostgreSQL
37	
38	    U->>V: navigate /owners/{id}
39	    V->>OR: owner by id
40	    OR->>DB: SELECT owner
41	    alt no row
42	        V-->>U: NotFoundException → NotFoundErrorView (404)
43	    else found
44	        V->>PR: pets of owner
45	        PR->>DB: SELECT pets JOIN types (ordered, GR-003)
46	        loop per pet
47	            V->>VR: visits of pet
48	            VR->>DB: SELECT visits (ordered, GR-003)
49	        end
50	        V-->>U: owner, pets, visit history
51	    end
52	```
53	
54	The per-pet loop is an accepted `1 + 1 + n` — `n` is the number of pets of one
55	owner, which is small and bounded. The lists that are *not* bounded never do
56	this; see *Query cost* below.
57	
58	## Searching — UC-004 Find Owners by Last Name
59	
60	```mermaid
61	sequenceDiagram
62	    actor U as Clinic User
63	    participant V as Find owners view
64	    participant R as Owner queries
65	    participant DB as PostgreSQL
66	
67	    U->>V: Find Owner ("Dav")
68	    V->>R: count owners with prefix
69	    R->>DB: SELECT count(*)
70	    alt count = 0
71	        V-->>U: "No owners found" (A1)
72	    else count = 1
73	        V-->>U: navigate to Owner Details (A2)
74	    else more than one
75	        V-->>U: render grid
76	        loop on every scroll step
77	            V->>R: page of owners (offset, limit)
78	            R->>DB: SELECT owners + multiset(pet names) OFFSET/LIMIT
79	        end
80	    end
81	```

88	    participant V as Add pet view
89	    participant F as Pet form
90	    participant R as Pet queries

92	
93	    U->>V: Add Pet
94	    V->>F: validate and read

96	        F-->>U: field errors, entries preserved
97	    else valid

99	        R->>DB: SELECT EXISTS (lower(name))

102	            F-->>U: error on the name field
103	        else free
104	            V->>R: insert(pet)
105	            R->>DB: INSERT (auto-commit)
106	            V-->>U: notification + navigate to Owner Details
107	        end

2	
3	Rules that more than one use case must honour.
4	
5	A rule that belongs to a single use case stays **in** that use case as
6	`BR-NNN` — it is part of that use case's story and has no life of its own. A
7	rule that several use cases share lives **here** as `GR-NNN`, is stated once,
8	and is referenced by each use case that applies it. The use case keeps its local
9	`BR-NNN` heading, so tests and the traceability sensors still point at a rule of
10	that use case; the heading says which shared rule it realizes instead of
11	restating it.
12	
13	`BusinessRuleTraceabilityTest` (`./mvnw test`) keeps the two sides honest: it
14	fails when a use case references a rule that does not exist, when a link lands
15	on a renamed heading, when the `**Realized by:**` line and the use cases
16	disagree in either direction, when the summary table drifts from the rules below
17	it, or when a rule here is realized by fewer than two use cases.
18	
19	**Why `GR` and not `BR`.** `BR-NNN` ids are scoped to a use case: every
20	`UC-NNN-*.md` numbers its rules from `BR-001`, and `@UseCase(businessRules =
21	"BR-001")` is resolved inside that one file. A global `BR-001` would therefore
22	stand beside ten local ones and mean nothing on its own. `GR` — global rule —
23	is a second namespace precisely so that an id never needs a use case to
24	disambiguate it.

29	| GR-002 | Lazy Loading of Lists            | UC-002 BR-001, UC-004 BR-002                 | NFR-001, NFR-002 |
30	| GR-003 | Deterministic Ordering           | UC-002 BR-002, UC-005 BR-001, UC-005 BR-002  | NFR-003 |

38	
39	Every screen the application offers is reachable without authentication. There
40	are no accounts and no login; the application is assumed to run on the clinic's
41	own trusted network.

45	## GR-002: Lazy Loading of Lists
46	
47	A list whose length grows with the size of the clinic's data is rendered with
48	infinite scrolling: rows are fetched from the backend as the user scrolls. There

{"type": "text", "text": "# Vaadin 25.2 Development Primer

Read this before writing Vaadin 25.2 code. It corrects the assumptions a model
trained on older material will otherwise make.

## Requirements

| Requirement | Version |
|---|---|
| Java | 21 or later |
| Spring Boot | **4.1 or later** |
| Jakarta EE | 11 |
| Node.js | 24 or later (Vaadin installs it) |
| Maven / Gradle | 3.8+ / 8.14+ |

Spring Boot 3.x and Spring Framework 6.x are **not supported** by any Vaadin 25
release. Spring Boot itself is optional — Vaadin runs without it.

## Added in 25.2

**Browser APIs, as server-side Java.** Do not hand-roll these with `executeJs`:
the wrappers handle the user-gesture requirement the browser enforces,
permission errors, and cleanup on detach. Documented under
`flow/browser-apis/`:

- `Geolocation` — `getPosition(…)` once, `watchPosition(…)` as a signal; sealed
  result types make permission-denied, unavailable and timeout exhaustive.
- `Clipboard` — `Clipboard.onClick(component)`, then write text, HTML or images;
  read and paste listeners too.
- `Fullscreen` — the page or a single component, current state as a signal.
- `WakeLock` — `request()` / `release()`, re-acquired when the tab returns.
- `WebShare` — the OS share sheet, with a signal reporting browser support.
- `ScreenOrientation` — orientation as a signal, plus `lock()` / `unlock()`.
- Page visibility — `UI.getPage().pageVisibilitySignal()`, distinguishing
  visible-and-focused, visible-but-unfocused and hidden.

Also new:

- `UI.triggerAfter(Duration, SerializableRunnable)` — a server-side task after a
  browser-side timer, **without enabling push**; the returned `Registration`
  cancels it.
- **Routing**: routes can declare a parent to form a hierarchy, page titles
  resolve for a route without instantiating it, and a router-state signal
  updates after every navigation — enough to drive breadcrumbs and menus.
- **Breadcrumbs** component; **Master Detail Layout**, **Slider** and **Badge**
  left preview. Slider's Flow API changed with it — 25.1's single `Slider` /
  `RangeSlider` became typed per value type — and Master Detail Layout also
  changed API since 25.1.
- `Html(String, SerializableSupplier<Safelist>)` sanitises untrusted HTML
  through jsoup instead of leaving it to the caller.
- Drop events carry coordinates (`DropEvent#getOffsetX()` / `getOffsetY()`).
- Bulk list-signal inserts (`ListSignal#insertAllFirst` and friends).
- `SessionLockListener` / `RpcInvocationListener` on `VaadinService`, for
  diagnosing lock contention.
- AI-assisted Charts and Grids, in preview (commercial). Frontend build on
  Vite 8.

## Two development models

Vaadin is a full-stack platform for business web applications in Java. Pick one
model per project; mixing is possible but only with a concrete reason.

- **Flow — server-side UI in Java.** The whole UI is Java; the framework keeps
  the browser in sync. The default unless React is explicitly requested.
- **Hilla — React/TypeScript UI, Java backend.** React views in
  `src/main/frontend/views/` (filename routing: `task-list.tsx` → `/task-list`,
  `@index.tsx` → `/`, `@layout.tsx` → the layout) call type-safe clients
  generated from `@BrowserCallable` Java services by
  `./mvnw compile vaadin:generate`. In Vaadin 25 Hilla is **opt-in**: add
  `hilla-spring-boot-starter`, no longer part of `vaadin-spring-boot-starter`.

Generate a new project at [start.vaadin.com](https://start.vaadin.com) (Maven,
Java 21) or from `https://start.vaadin.com/skeleton`. Run it with
`./mvnw spring-boot:run`.

**On an existing project, follow the patterns already in it.** For a new one,
Vaadin promotes feature-based packaging — `base/`, `security/`, and one package
per feature holding its own `domain/`, `service/` and `ui/view/` — rather than
layers.
